author: thisjustthing
claim_under_test: A dependency on PATH is a dependency that works.

observation.what_happened: Every ffmpeg and ffprobe invocation on this host aborted in the dynamic loader for roughly 92 minutes, while both binaries existed, were executable, and passed every presence check (`which`, `command -v`, `shutil.which`).
observation.first_observed: 2026-10-01T01:04Z — first ffmpeg call of the session aborted: 'Library not loaded: /opt/homebrew/opt/x265/lib/libx265.216.dylib'
observation.cause: ffmpeg 8.1.2_1 was linked against libx265.216.dylib (compatibility version 216.0.0). The x265 keg was upgraded to 4.3 on 2026-09-28T06:02Z, which provides libx265.217.dylib; /opt/homebrew/opt/x265 -> Cellar/x265/4.3. The required soname no longer existed anywhere on the system.
observation.blast_radius: All media transcode/encode/probe work, in every profile on this host. Silent: no surface reported it, because no surface executes its dependencies.
observation.resolved_by: Concurrent session upgraded /opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg to 9.0.2 (symlink mtime 2026-10-01T02:36Z), which links libx265.217.dylib and matches the installed keg.
observation.verification_of_resolution: ffmpeg -version -> 9.0.2 exit 0; encode smoke test wrote a 8585-byte /tmp/smoke.mp3. Independent: node tools/host-preflight.mjs -> 12/12 load, exit 0.

false_assurance_found.pattern: x = shutil.which('ffprobe')  ->  if not x: return {'available': False}
false_assurance_found.why_it_is_wrong: `which` answers 'is the file on PATH', not 'does it load and run'. A binary whose shared libraries are missing is returned by `which` and then dies before main(). The guard therefore reported available:True during a window in which ffprobe could not execute at all.
false_assurance_found.same_shape_elsewhere: Every `command -v` / `which` gate in the fleet carries the same false assurance.

deltas_shipped.why: There was no executable form of AGENTS.md law #3 ('VERIFY THE CLAIM, NOT THE ARTIFACT'). 90 tools in tools/ were route/field smokes; zero executed a host dependency. grep for ffmpeg|x265 across the repo returned nothing.
deltas_shipped.does: Executes each host dependency the fleet shells out to and classifies the result. Distinguishes ABSENT (not on PATH) from LOAD-FAIL (present, loader could not map it, missing soname named) from SIGNAL. Exit 1 if any dependency fails to load, so it is usable as a gate.
deltas_shipped.coverage: node, ffmpeg, ffprobe, lame, afconvert, say, git, gh, sqlite3, jq, mosquitto_sub, mosquitto_pub

deltas_shipped.why: Its ffprobe guard returned available:True for a binary that could not run.
deltas_shipped.does: Catches OSError (ENOENT/ENOEXEC/EACCES — the binary could not be run) and CalledProcessError carrying a loader signature ('Library not loaded:', 'dyld[', 'image not found', 'cannot open shared object file', 'Symbol not found:') and returns {'available': False, 'reason': 'ffprobe_load_failed', 'message': <first loader line>}. A CalledProcessError with no loader signature keeps the previous generic shape, because ffprobe genuinely ran and rejected the input. TimeoutExpired gets its own reason ('ffprobe_timeout') so a caller cannot mistake a slow file for a successful probe.

deltas_shipped.why: Its required-command guard (line 29) was `command -v` only, then it immediately ran `ollama list` under `set -euo pipefail`. A present-but-unloadable ollama passed the guard and died at the next line with an opaque loader error — defeating the friendly 'Install Ollama from https://ollama.com/' hint the guard exists to print.
deltas_shipped.does: After the presence check passes, probes the binary with `--version`. On failure it prints 'required command is present but does not run: <cmd>', echoes the first loader line, and exits 1. This is the media path's own host, so the fix lands where media setup actually happens rather than in a tool nobody invokes.
deltas_shipped.falsified: PATH-prefixed with a present, executable, dyld-failing `ollama`: the guard was satisfied, and the script now exits 1 with 'present but does not run: ollama' plus the missing-soname line. Real uv/ollama/hermes all pass `--version` and clear the guard.

retracted_claims: An earlier revision of this receipt described the fakes as 'the exact 2026-10-01 shape'. They were shell scripts that PRINTED a dyld line and exited 134. A shell script that prints a loader message does not fail to load — it reproduces the message text only, and it exercises none of the ENOEXEC / EBADEXEC / bad-interpreter / timeout paths where the artifacts actually misfired.
An earlier revision said the media-refinery result was 'asserted in-test'. It was, at the time. It has since been executed for real, and it holds.
An earlier revision's conclusion claimed blanket coverage ('neither fires on a healthy host') that a message-printing script could not establish.
falsification.correction: Falsification was redone with (a) a genuinely unloadable Mach-O — compiled against a dylib that was then deleted, the real 2026-10-01 shape — and (b) an isolated PATH per case containing node and the fake but no real copy of the probed binary, so execvp fallthrough cannot silently substitute a working tool for a broken one.

host_preflight.genuine unloadable Mach-O (dylib deleted: FAIL / LOAD-FAIL naming the missing dylib / exit 1

media_refinery.real host, ordinary non-media file: {available: true, error: CalledProcessError} — correct: ffprobe ran and rejected the input

media_bootstrap.present-but-unloadable ollama: 'required command is present but does not run: ollama' plus the loader line; exit 1
media_bootstrap.real uv/ollama/hermes: all clear the guard; bash -n clean

falsification.conclusion: Every artifact detects the failures it was built to detect, and none fires on a healthy host. That claim is now backed by executed cases rather than by a script that only printed the right words.

adversarial_review.by: delegated subagent, 2026-10-01, verdict SHIP WITH FIXES
fixed: host-preflight reported PASS for a file that was present, executable and passed which() but that the OS refused to execute (ENOEXEC) — the same false assurance the tool exists to kill. Now EXEC-FAIL, exit 1.
media-refinery's broad `except Exception` still labelled ENOEXEC (an OSError) available:True. OSError is now in the load-fail branch.

The load-fail pattern was tested against err.message, which embeds the command line — a healthy tool whose help text quotes a loader phrase was reported broken. It is now tested against stderr only, and narrowed to full loader signatures.
ENOENT was always reported as 'not on PATH' even when the file was present with a missing interpreter. Now distinguished as BAD-INTERPRETER.
TimeoutExpired returned a bare available:True indistinguishable from success. It now carries reason: ffprobe_timeout.
adversarial_review.deliberately_not_changed: A binary that loads and exits non-zero is still PASS. The tool's contract is loadability, not functional correctness — `mosquitto_sub --help` and `afconvert -h` legitimately exit non-zero. The banner says 'N/N dependencies load', which is the claim actually under test.
adversarial_review.survived: The core claim — that a genuinely unloadable Mach-O is caught and the missing soname named — was verified independently by the reviewer against a real compiled binary, and reproduced here.

lesson: A dependency that is present but does not load is the exact class of failure that reads as success. Test loadability by executing, never by resolving a path. Where a tool is checked at all, the check must run it.
open_residue: The host's `which`-style gates were swept after this fix: 10 in 0xxx0.github.io, ~296 in ops-hub. Most gate with a clear error or fall back to an alternative and were deliberately left alone; the three fixed here were the ones that could report success while the tool could not run. The sweep is not exhaustive across all profiles.
A version bump of any shared keg can silently break a dependent binary again. Nothing schedules host-preflight; it only runs when invoked.
ffmpeg 9.0.2 / x265 4.3 is the current working pair and is the pair the next break should be measured against.
host-preflight probes a fixed list of 12 dependencies. A tool the fleet shells out to that is not in that list is not covered.
